correctness.rationale: The three families are the lines of the complex degree-p Fermat surface; substituting their equations gives the same-family rook rule and the three cross congruences, with the +1 in the A–C rule because λ²=ζ. The graph is connected, of degree 4p−2. Over F_p the two fixed axis directions give the diagonal 2 of EHEᵀ and the three exchanged diagonal-fiber pairs give the cross adjacencies, so L=−EHEᵀ. Function evaluation in a,b is injective for polynomials of separate degrees below p. In each family the four degree-k ridge forms have ranks 1,2,3 at k=0,1,2 and rank four thereafter (use the coefficients of a^k,b^k,a^(k−1)b,a^(k−2)b²); thus K=ker E has dimension 18 with fiber polynomials of degree at most two. Since im Eᵀ=K^⊥ and H is an involution, the lost rank from im Eᵀ upon applying EH is exactly the radical dimension of H restricted to K. For p≥7, each pairing is a sum of degree-at-most-four polynomials, zero in F_p, giving rank 12p−36. Fresh direct elimination at p=3 and p=5 independently returned 7 and 26, giving the required exceptions. A connected graph has one free summand in its full integral Laplacian cokernel, so n−1−rank(L mod p) yields precisely the stated p-ranks.
residual_risks: The finite replay uses the stated incidence predicates, not an independent classification of the complex projective lines. The result says nothing about geometric lines in characteristic p, or the complete integral or p-primary Smith form.
